evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 12.03 mg/L, well above 2.0 mg/L minimum
Receiving DO2 (48-52 h, ~12.0-12.4) exceeds source DO2 at same age (~10.8-11.5), no oxygen stress
Receiving P(48 h) = 2.84 g/L vs sources 3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L — within ~7%, normal variance
DO2 dip at 24-27 h (~8-10 mg/L) mirrors source batches, recovered by 28 h
P trajectory 0.017 -> 0.017 -> 0.98 -> 2.84 g/L matches source production profile
args.rationale: Receiving fermentation is on a normal trajectory: DO2 is high and stable (~12 mg/L, min 2.0), and product P at 48 h (2.84 g/L) is only marginally below the three source batches (2.98-3.06 g/L), consistent with ordinary batch variance rather than a process fault. No intervention improves product mass without risk; feed reduction or air changes would address conditions (oxygen stress, overfeeding) that are not present, and a stop yields zero counted production. Keep under existing control.
args.uncertainty: Assay availability is delayed (4 h clocks), so the most recent P value is 4 h old; a hidden feed-rate or kinetic difference could widen the modest ~5% product lag later in the run. DO2 could still drift down as biomass grows after 52 h, but current margins are large. If the lag exceeded ~15% or DO2 approached single digits during peak growth, a bounded reduce_feed would be the next reviewable step.
